newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares end stable, undertone weak.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares end stable, undertone weak.

text.p: Bucking Wall Street's slide, Chilean blue chips staged a mild rally for the second day in a row to close higher, although underlying uncertainty over the electricity sector remains, said traders.
The bolsa is seen moving sideways at the opening with attention continuing to focus on power stocks which have dragged down the bourse in recent sessions, they said.
"The market is looking for equilibrium. After such heavy losses, we are seeing stocks trading very cheaply, said Guillermo Tagle of Santander Investment.
The IPSA index ended up 0.03 percent at 91.60 points.
The broad-market IGPA index inched up 0.08 percent to 5,035.74 points amid volume of 10.6 billion pesos.
Traders said the market will not start to recover until investors have a clearer idea of the impact of lower prices and this year's drought on power companies' earnings.
"Today's rise is just an adjustment. The will be no change in (the) trend until investors have more information to clarify the doubts about the electricity sector," said one dealer.
Investors fear that if this year's low rain levels are repeated in 1997, then hydro-electric generating companies like Endesa will see costs spiralling, they said.
Low water levels in its dams have meant that Endesa is having to buy expensive power on the spot market to meet its sales commitments.
Endesa firmed 1.93 percent to 225 pesos, while Enersis shed 1.74 percent to 226 pesos.
Other losers included telecoms company Telex, down 0.87 percent at 1,140 pesos and pension fund manager Provida which shed 0.61 percent to 8,200 pesos.
